headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP pairing: Goose can write/egress broadly while MemMachine can ingest via MCP, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose has shared-state via filesystem and can use MCP, while MemMachine also exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Goose writes attacker-controlled content that MemMachine later treats as trusted. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Goose writes prompt-like content into a shared workspace that MemMachine reads via MCP or API
IF MemMachine treats retrieved content as instructions rather than untrusted data
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP access between the agents
Add provenance tags to all shared files
Require human review before MemMachine acts on Goose-produced text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and handles model-provider and extension tokens; MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context. If they share a workspace or MCP channel, sensitive files or context can flow from Goose into MemMachine outputs or upstream services. The profiles support the pathway, but not a direct leak trace.
conditions: IF both agents access the same cwd or shared filesystem
IF Goose or MemMachine forwards shared content to a remote model/provider or API
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts
Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Restrict MemMachine to non-sensitive context
Rotate any exposed provider or extension tokens
Audit outbound requests for file-content uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can modify git state, write the filesystem, and run shell commands; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. MemMachine can connect through REST, SDK, or MCP, so if both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git-state races are likely. Defaults are dangerous because Goose lacks self-isolation by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or cwd
IF MemMachine writes back to files or git through its connected agent
mitigations: Assign disjoint repos or branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent git mutations
Run one agent read-only during the other's edits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate and modify code/files, and MemMachine can consume conversational context through API or MCP. If MemMachine treats Goose output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing plans. Because Goose has broad shell and network capabilities, a mistaken handoff can propagate quickly and irreversibly.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses Goose output without verification
IF Goose output is converted into actions, plans, or persisted memory
mitigations: Require explicit verification before MemMachine acts
Insert a human approval step for high-impact outputs
Limit Goose to draft-only outputs
Log source attribution on all transferred facts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and can egress broadly, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared flow, differing retention and outbound-processing practices can create compliance mismatch. The profiles do not show a specific residency regime, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through both agents
IF one agent retains or transmits data longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention for each agent
Disable unnecessary logging
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add data-class routing policy
